title: Rabbi Drosa – Drosi – Drostai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman finds him mentioned only in the Jerusalem Talmud and the Midrashim, as in Shabbat, beginning of halakhah 2 of chapter 1: “Rabbi Drosa said: So it was; Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose (he is the Amora) said: He was an appointed agent.” In Kilayim, beginning of halakhah 3 of chapter 9: “Rabbi Drosa said (regarding what Rabbi commanded, ‘My widow shall not move from my house’): so that they would not say to her, ‘It is the house of the Nesiut; it is subject to the Nesiut.’ Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose said: Like what was taught,” etc. In Ketubot, chapter 12, the reading is Rabbi Dosa. Likewise in Taanit 4:2: “Rabbi Dros′ said: Because they cry out against him … Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Yose said: Because he offered a reply in public.” Hyman infers from this that he was like a colleague of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose.

In Sanhedrin, end of chapter 7: “Rabbi Drosa said: There were nine hundred sections,” etc. In Shemot Rabbah 43:4: “Rabbi Drosai said: He made himself a chair,” etc. In Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:11: “Rabbi Drosa and Rabbi Yirmeyah in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said: Six hundred thousand prophets arose for Israel in the days of Eliyahu.” Midrash Shmuel 28:4 reads “Rabbi Daostai and Rabbi Yirmeyah in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai”; Hyman proposes the reading in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, and he also suggests “Rabbi Yirmeyah” without the vav. In Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 4:4 we find Rabbi Petoroki, the brother of Rabbi Drosa.

notes.text: נשיות is the patriarchate (Nesiut), not women; saved Guggenheimer Kilayim9:3 and English Ketubot12:3 support that reading. The widow is being addressed about the institutional house. Supplied שהושיבו טעם is read in the sense of a public reply; named Guggenheimer Taanit4:2 has שהשיבו טעם and the connected Chanina/Rabbi pronunciation-correction episode. Hyman’s colleague and name corrections stay attributed.

Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3 directly names Drosa and the institutional Nesiut house. The consulted Taanit 4:2 has “he answered him publicly” and the connected pronunciation-correction account; Hyman’s supplied wording and colleague inference remain his. Other name and transmission-chain corrections are not silently harmonized.
